slides.title: Optional extension
slides.html:
Optional review repeat of 4.10 Day 2: the other two SSS cases.

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Case 2: CG meets line AB outside segment AB.Same setup as the 4.10 proof.
Subtract the equal base angles instead of adding them. You still get angle ACB = angle AGB.Theorem 9, then angle subtraction.
Case 3: CG passes through A or B, so A, C, G (or B, C, G) are on one line.Only one isosceles triangle remains.
That one isosceles triangle gives angle ACB = angle AGB directly.Theorem 9.
In every case, SAS finishes the proof.So SSS holds for all triangles.

slides.title: Review item 1
slides.html:
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle PQR. Which side matches CA?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

RP, by C↔R,A↔P.

Reveal second check

third-first positions match.

geo.title: Review item 1
geo.prompt: Triangle ABC ≅ triangle PQR. Which side matches CA?

slides.title: Review item 2
slides.html:
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF, BC = 2x + 3 and EF = 15. Find x.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

2x+3=15,2x=12,x=6.

Reveal second check

2(6)+3=15.

geo.title: Review item 2
geo.prompt: Triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF, BC = 2x + 3 and EF = 15. Find x.

slides.title: Review item 3
slides.html:
AB = DE, AC = DF and angle A = angle D. Which test?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

SAS, since A,D are between the given sides.

Reveal second check

ray-alignment motion fixes both endpoints.

geo.title: Review item 3
geo.prompt: AB = DE, AC = DF and angle A = angle D. Which test?
geo.solution: SAS, since A,D are between the given sides.

slides.title: Review item 4
slides.html:
Angle A = angle D, angle B = angle E and AB = DE. Which test?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

ASA, since AB,DE join the given-angle vertices.

Reveal second check

two endpoint rays have one intersection.

geo.title: Review item 4
geo.prompt: Angle A = angle D, angle B = angle E and AB = DE. Which test?
geo.solution: ASA, since AB,DE join the given-angle vertices.
geo.check: two endpoint rays have one intersection.

slides.title: Review item 5
slides.html:
Two segments AD and BC cross at M, and M is the midpoint of both. Prove triangle AMB ≅ triangle DMC.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

AM=DM,BM=CM by midpoint; AMB=DMC by vertical angles; SAS.

Reveal second check

A↔D,M↔M,B↔C makes all three facts corresponding.

geo.title: Review item 5
geo.prompt: Two segments AD and BC cross at M, and M is the midpoint of both. Prove triangle AMB ≅ triangle DMC.
geo.solution: AM=DM,BM=CM by midpoint; AMB=DMC by vertical angles; SAS.
geo.check: A↔D,M↔M,B↔C makes all three facts corresponding.

slides.title: Review item 6
slides.html:
Once triangle AMB ≅ triangle DMC, which side matches AB?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

DC, so AB=DC by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

first-third positions agree.

geo.title: Review item 6
geo.prompt: Once triangle AMB ≅ triangle DMC, which side matches AB?

slides.title: Review item 7
slides.html:
AB = AC, angle B = (3x + 2) degrees and angle C = (5x - 16) degrees. Find x and the base angles.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

3x+2=5x-16 gives x=9 and both angles 29.

Reveal second check

27+2=45-16=29.

geo.title: Review item 7
geo.prompt: AB = AC, angle B = (3x + 2) degrees and angle C = (5x - 16) degrees. Find x and the base angles.

slides.title: Review item 8
slides.html:
In triangle ABC, angle B = angle C. Prove AB = AC.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Compare ABC with ACB; B=C,C=B,BC=CB imply ASA,then AB=AC by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

all used results precede SSS.

geo.title: Review item 8
geo.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle B = angle C. Prove AB = AC.
geo.solution: Compare ABC with ACB; B=C,C=B,BC=CB imply ASA,then AB=AC by CPCTC.

slides.title: Review item 9
slides.html:
Does matching all three angles (AAA) prove two triangles congruent?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. Side-2 and side-5 equilateral triangles have matching angles but unequal sides.

Reveal second check

isometries cannot map length 2 to 5.

geo.title: Review item 9
geo.prompt: Does matching all three angles (AAA) prove two triangles congruent?
geo.solution: No. Side-2 and side-5 equilateral triangles have matching angles but unequal sides.

slides.title: Review item 10
slides.html:
A proof uses CPCTC before it proves the triangles congruent. Fix the order.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

First give SAS/ASA facts, then conclude congruence, then use CPCTC.

Reveal second check

CPCTC hypothesis is now established.

geo.title: Review item 10
geo.prompt: A proof uses CPCTC before it proves the triangles congruent. Fix the order.
geo.solution: First give SAS/ASA facts, then conclude congruence, then use CPCTC.

slides.title: Review item 11
slides.html:
In convex quadrilateral ABCD, AB = AD and BC = DC. Prove AC bisects angle BAD.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

AB=AD,BC=DC,AC=AC imply ABC≅ADC by SSS; BAC=DAC by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

A↔A,B↔D,C↔C is the ordered match.

geo.title: Review item 11
geo.prompt: In convex quadrilateral ABCD, AB = AD and BC = DC. Prove AC bisects angle BAD.
geo.solution: AB=AD,BC=DC,AC=AC imply ABC≅ADC by SSS; BAC=DAC by CPCTC.

slides.title: Review item 12
slides.html:
Three pairs of equal sides are given, and no angles. Can you use SAS right away?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. Use SSS.

Reveal second check

SAS requires an included-angle equality not among the givens.

geo.title: Review item 12
geo.prompt: Three pairs of equal sides are given, and no angles. Can you use SAS right away?
geo.check: SAS requires an included-angle equality not among the givens.

slides.title: Review item 13
slides.html:
Circles centered at D and E are 5 apart, with radii 4 and 3. Why do both crossing points copy the same triangle?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Both give DF=4,EF=3,DE=5; SSS proves congruence.

Reveal second check

reflection in DE exchanges intersections.

geo.title: Review item 13
geo.prompt: Circles centered at D and E are 5 apart, with radii 4 and 3. Why do both crossing points copy the same triangle?
geo.solution: Both give DF=4,EF=3,DE=5; SSS proves congruence.

slides.title: Review item 14
slides.html:
Circles of the same radius at A and B cross at P and Q. What must you define before you talk about M?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

M=PQ∩AB. With P,Q opposite sides and common radius>AB/2,M lies between A,B.

Reveal second check

A half-turn about the midpoint of AB exchanges P and Q, so the midpoint is also on PQ.

geo.solution: M=PQ∩AB. With P,Q opposite sides and common radius>AB/2,M lies between A,B.
geo.check: A half-turn about the midpoint of AB exchanges P and Q, so the midpoint is also on PQ.

slides.title: Review item 15
slides.html:
AB = 10 and the radius is 5. Can the crossing points give a perpendicular bisector?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. Tangency yields one point.

Reveal second check

radius must strictly exceed half of 10.

geo.title: Review item 15
geo.prompt: AB = 10 and the radius is 5. Can the crossing points give a perpendicular bisector?
geo.check: radius must strictly exceed half of 10.

slides.title: Review item 16
slides.html:
Look at the figure. C1 and C2 are on the same ray from A, AB = 5, AC1 = 3 and AC2 = 5. C1 and C2 lie on the same circle centered at B. Explain why SSA fails here, without trig.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Same rays give equal angle A,AB common,and circle centered B through both C vertices gives BC1=BC2. But AC1=3≠5=AC2.

Reveal second check

side multisets differ.

geo.title: Review item 16
geo.prompt: Look at the figure. C1 and C2 are on the same ray from A, AB = 5, AC1 = 3 and AC2 = 5. C1 and C2 lie on the same circle centered at B. Explain why SSA fails here, without trig.
geo.solution: Same rays give equal angle A,AB common,and circle centered B through both C vertices gives BC1=BC2. But AC1=3≠5=AC2.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html: Keep vertex order matched. Establish congruence before CPCTC. AAA and SSA are not tests. SSS is proved here, not assumed. Define every point and check that circles cross twice.
